DK912B Korttarmssyndrom is a WHO-classified diagnosis code utilized within the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] (DANIBD) to identify patients suffering from short bowel syndrome [^src1]. This condition is recognized as a severe complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and is tracked in patient characterizations as a rare but clinically significant diagnosis [^src1]. 

In the context of DANIBD's national efforts to systematize and improve IBD treatment in Denmark, standardized coding like DK912B allows for detailed quality monitoring, clinical benchmarking, and the evaluation of treatment guidelines [^src1]. The code appears in the registry's appendix tables, which detail patient characteristics and epidemiological data. For the reporting period covered in the 2023 annual report (October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023), the code was associated with specific patient counts across different categories, recorded as "28 (0) 6 (0) 13 (0) 34 (0) 7 (0)" [^src1]. In the subsequent 2024 report, the code is again listed in the appendix tables for quality indicators, showing a recorded value of "20 (0)" [^src2]. These data points contribute to the broader quantitative foundation used to evaluate surgical interventions, comorbidities, and the implementation of quality indicators in Danish IBD care [^src2].
